U.S. equities advanced on October 21, 2026, with the broad market up 0.36 percent on the session. The rally was driven primarily by artificial intelligence sentiment, as Reuters reported that SpaceX results reignited the AI trade. Wall Street Journal coverage highlighted that Meta is getting creative to fund its massive AI investments and will split stock to create a new class for that purpose. The Nasdaq-100 outperformed with a 0.65 percent gain, compared to 0.33 percent for the S&P 500 and 0.47 percent for the Dow Jones, reflecting strength in technology-focused equities.

Information Technology and Technology sectors led the advance, gaining 1.65 and 1.48 percent respectively, while Industrials added 0.92 percent. Among gainers, Skydance Corporation surged 10.85 percent following directors and dealings activity reported by Financial Times. Supermicro climbed 9.55 percent and SpaceX rose 7.79 percent, both contributing to the AI sentiment boost cited by Reuters. Charles River Laboratories gained 9.33 percent, MicroStrategy added 7.54 percent, and Datadog rose 6.5 percent on analyst calls noted by CNBC. Illumina, Inc. advanced 5.57 percent after Financial Times reported the expansion of its BioInsight Platform with new software. EchoStar, Bloom Energy, and Ciena also posted gains of 7.23, 7.13, and 5.67 percent respectively.

Consumer-oriented sectors retreated, with Consumer Staples down 0.82 percent and Consumer Discretionary off 0.81 percent. AT&T fell 6.45 percent with no tracked catalyst reported. Dexcom declined 6.39 percent, Netflix dropped 5.31 percent on theatrical expansion questions covered by CNBC, and Chipotle Mexican Grill slid 5.16 percent as Barron's reported on soft sales and pricing pressure. Expedia Group fell 5.03 percent, DoorDash lost 3.77 percent, and Lululemon Athletica declined 3.41 percent, all without specific company catalysts tracked by the outlets surveyed. Booking Holdings fell 3.38 percent after Reuters reported the company was targeted in an EU investigation into phishing scams and fraudulent listings. SBA Communications and PDD Holdings also posted declines of 4.18 and 3.56 percent respectively.

El Niño Stresses China’s Power Market With Return to Costly Gas
Musk sets lower sales target for Tesla as it explores SpaceX merger

markets_brief.prose_html: Tesla ha riportato utili e vendite superiori alle attese nonostante un calo dei ricavi automotive, mentre Elon Musk ha segnalato un target di vendite più basso mentre l'azienda esplora una fusione con SpaceX. Nel frattempo, le pressioni infrastrutturali si stanno intensificando in Asia: il boom dei data center in India attira scrutinio per il consumo di acqua e energia, mentre le condizioni di El Niño stanno mettendo sotto stress il mercato energetico cinese e spingono un costoso ritorno alla generazione da gas. Le tensioni geopolitiche hanno pesato anche sul sentiment con gli Stati Uniti che hanno ordinato il ritiro di personale dall'Arabia Saudita a seguito degli attacchi Houthi.
markets_brief.prose_html_en: Tesla delivered better-than-expected earnings and sales despite a decline in auto revenue, while Elon Musk signaled a lower sales target as the company explores a merger with SpaceX. Separately, infrastructure pressures are mounting across Asia: India's data center boom is drawing scrutiny over water and power consumption, while El Niño conditions are straining China's power market and driving a costly return to gas generation. Geopolitical tensions also weighed on sentiment as the US ordered personnel withdrawals from Saudi Arabia following Houthi attacks.
